speaker: René Schubert
affiliation: GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel, Germany
bio: René Schubert is an ocean dynamicist with a focus on ocean scale interactions from numerical models, theory, and observations. His work concentrated on the near-surface kinetic energy cascade of submesoscale, mesoscale and large-scale flows from satellite measurements and numerical models, and on the effects of large-scale instabilities and resulting interior eddies on the abyssal circulation and the formation of benthic storms from moored data and ocean models. After a doctorate and a first postdoc at GEOMAR (Kiel), he did a second postdoc at LOPS (Brest) with extensive collaborations with UCLA, then moved back to GEOMAR in the ERC synergy project WHIRLS, where he investigates submesoscale ocean dynamics and associated air-sea interactions.
talkTitle: The ocean flows downhill near the seafloor and recirculates upward above
abstract: The abyssal ocean, in the lowest 1000 m above the seafloor, moves on average with the deeper seafloor to its left in the Northern Hemisphere and to its right in the Southern Hemisphere. Using current-meter measurements and numerical simulations, we show that the interior flow, O(100 m) to O(1000 m) above the seafloor, is deflected within the bottom boundary layer into a widespread downhill flow which intensifies with the steepness of the seafloor. Typical local changes in seafloor steepness lead to a shallow divergence and a deep convergence of this downhill flow, connected by an overlying upward recirculation forming closed overturning cells that extend on average over the lowest 1000 m of the ocean. As oceanic overturning is climate-relevant, these impacts need to be better understood and represented in climate and Earth system simulations.
